speakers.name: Dr. Rajendra Prasad
speakers.positionSummary: Closes the Objectives Resolution debate, conducts the standing vote, moves the House to Bhutan and Sikkim, and manages the transition to the Assembly budget.

speakers.name: H. J. Khandekar
speakers.positionSummary: Suggests that a declaration associated with independence should be adopted on Independence Day, 26 January.

speakers.name: Syamanandan Sahaya
speakers.positionSummary: Withdraws the two amendments standing in his name, leaving the Resolution to proceed without surviving amendments.

speakers.name: Several Members
speakers.positionSummary: Collectively consent to Sahaya's withdrawal request and participate in the standing vote.

speakers.name: Jawaharlal Nehru
speakers.positionSummary: Closes six weeks of argument by keeping the door open to absent groups while insisting constitution-making can no longer wait, then moves the Bhutan-Sikkim resolution.

speakers.name: Mohan Lal Saksena
speakers.positionSummary: Reads the Urdu translation of the Objectives Resolution before the final vote.

speakers.name: Govind Ballabh Pant
speakers.positionSummary: Seconds Nehru's motion extending the States Negotiating Committee's scope to Bhutan and Sikkim.

speakers.name: H. V. Kamath
speakers.positionSummary: Asks that the Assembly not transact business the next day as a tribute on Subhas Chandra Bose's golden jubilee.

speakers.name: N. V. Gadgil
speakers.positionSummary: Moves sanction of the Assembly's estimated expenditure for 1946–47 and 1947–48.

speakers.name: K. Santhanam
speakers.positionSummary: Moves that the Assembly budget be considered in Committee and in camera.

speakers.name: Sri Biswanath Das
speakers.positionSummary: Supports taking the budget discussion into Committee.

speakers.name: Somnath Lahiri
speakers.positionSummary: Objects to excluding visitors because the matter concerns public money.

speakers.name: B. G. Kher
speakers.positionSummary: Participates in the procedural exchange as the House becomes Committee for the budget discussion.

interventions.summary: The President sets out three items: completion of the Objectives Resolution, a resolution on Bhutan and Sikkim, and the Assembly budget. He asks whether the House is ready for closure and Nehru's final reply.
Khandekar proposes passing the Resolution on 26 January, associating the constitutional declaration with Independence Day.
Syamanandan Sahaya asks leave to withdraw both amendments standing in his name.
The Chair places Sahaya's request before the House.
Members agree, clearing the way for the main Resolution to be decided without surviving amendments.

Nehru says postponement served a legitimate purpose by giving absent parties and the country time to consider the Resolution. The invitation to join remains open, but the Assembly's work cannot stay suspended indefinitely.
He turns from constitutional form to social purpose: freeing India through a new Constitution must also confront hunger, poverty and lack of opportunity.
interventions.excerpt: all our paper constitutions will become useless and purposeless

interventions.summary: Nehru rejects princely objections to authority deriving from the people. Cooperation with Britain or the Commonwealth, he adds, cannot diminish India's independence.
He rejects waiting until 26 January merely for symbolic timing.

Nehru places the Resolution in a longer chain of independence pledges, accepts the wisdom of the six-week postponement, but says the balance has shifted to action. Absent members remain welcome, yet future work will proceed whether or not they join.
He presents the Resolution as friendship rather than hostility and connects constitutional freedom with food, clothing, housing, opportunity and India's responsibilities in Asia and the world.
Rajendra Prasad asks members to recognise the solemnity of the pledge, reads the Resolution into the record and gives its Hindi translation.
At the President's request, Mohan Lal Saksena reads the Urdu translation.
The President calls on members to stand in favour. The Objectives Resolution is adopted with all members standing.
The House turns to the resolution concerning Bhutan and Sikkim and the President calls Nehru.

Nehru moves to enlarge the States Negotiating Committee's mandate so it can examine the special problems of Bhutan and Sikkim and report to the Assembly. He recalls the committee created on 21 December and its original mandate over State representation.
Govind Ballabh Pant seconds the Bhutan-Sikkim resolution.
With no member seeking to speak, the Chair puts the resolution to the House and it is adopted.
Kamath asks the House not to transact business the next day as a tribute marking Subhas Chandra Bose's golden jubilee.
The President says no business is ready for the next day, so the Assembly will have a holiday in any case.
Gadgil moves sanction of the Assembly's estimated expenditure for 1946–47 and 1947–48 and begins explaining the estimates.
Santhanam moves that the budget be taken up in Committee rather than in the presence of visitors.
N. G. Ranga seconds Santhanam's motion.
Biswanath Das also supports taking the budget discussion into Committee.
Somnath Lahiri objects that the matter concerns public money and questions why discussion should not remain public.
The President separates the budget motion from the question of meeting in Committee, then takes the sense of the House.
The procedural exchange ends with the House proceeding to consider the budget in Committee and the public galleries being cleared for the in-camera discussion recorded by the source.
